response.sql: WITH ratios AS (SELECT p.SEX, CAST(l.CPK AS REAL) / l.GPT AS ratio FROM Patient p JOIN Laboratory l ON p.ID = l.ID WHERE p.SEX IS NOT NULL AND l.CPK IS NOT NULL AND l.GPT IS NOT NULL AND l.GPT != 0), sex_avgs AS (SELECT SEX, AVG(ratio) AS avg_ratio FROM ratios GROUP BY SEX), m1 AS (SELECT AVG(avg_ratio) AS mean1 FROM sex_avgs), s1 AS (SELECT SEX, avg_ratio FROM sex_avgs, m1 WHERE avg_ratio > m1.mean1), m2 AS (SELECT AVG(avg_ratio) AS mean2 FROM s1), s2 AS (SELECT avg_ratio FROM s1, m2 WHERE avg_ratio > m2.mean2), final_avg AS (SELECT AVG(avg_ratio) AS result FROM s2) SELECT final_avg.result, final_avg.result - m1.mean1, final_avg.result - m2.mean2 FROM final_avg, m1, m2

assumptions.assumption: Tests where CPK or GPT is NULL or GPT = 0 are excluded (ratio undefined)
Only non-NULL SEX values are grouped; NULL sex values are excluded from analysis
Two sequential filters: (1) retain SEX values whose average exceeds the overall mean of all sex averages, (2) among retained sexes, retain only those exceeding the mean of the first-filter result

alternatives.interpretation: Single-stage filter: retain SEX values whose average exceeds the overall mean; 'above their own mean' is descriptive or erroneous phrasing, and 'second mean' is simply the first mean again
